turns.doctor_question: Hello, what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just keep going back over my jobs again and again. I'm an electrician, and I find myself checking the breakers, the panel labels, torque marks... I even take photos of everything just to be sure. Sometimes I'll even drive all the way back to a job site after I've already left just to look at it again. 

It's getting to the point where a simple install takes way longer than it should, and, honestly, people at work are starting to notice.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly describes repetitive, excessive checking behaviors (re-checking electrical panels, taking photos, and driving back to job sites) that interfere with work efficiency.

turns.doctor_question: What do you fear might happen, or what feeling do you get, if you try to leave without checking again?
turns.patient_response: If I try to just leave... well, even after I know for a fact I checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought just keeps barging in on me. I get this overwhelming fear that maybe I missed one loose neutral, or that I left something in a way that could start a fire. I try to shake it off, I really do, but the thought just follows me all the way home. It just doesn't go away.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes intrusive, persistent thoughts and doubts about having missed a loose neutral or starting a fire, which they attempt to shake off but cannot dismiss.

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience the checking as unwanted and excessive, or does it feel like a reasonable and necessary part of doing the job correctly?
turns.patient_response:
I know it's excessive. I mean... safety is a big part of the job, obviously, so double-checking your work is normal. But what I'm doing is way past that. 

I really don't want to be doing it. It's frustrating because I know in my head that the work is fine and I already looked at it, but I end up doing the checks anyway just to get the fear to stop. So, yeah, it definitely feels unwanted.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in excessive, repetitive checking behaviors that they recognize are beyond normal safety checks, performed specifically to make their fear stop.

turns.doctor_question: How long has this pattern of intrusive fears and repeated checking been going on?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure of the exact timeline, to be honest. It's just... it's been happening for a while now, but I couldn't give you a specific date or anything when it started. It kind of just crept up on me.

turns.doctor_question: Have these intrusive fears and repeated checking behaviors been present on most days for at least two weeks?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I mean... I don't keep a log of it or anything, but yes. It's definitely been at least two weeks. It happens pretty much every day I'm on a job site lately.

turns.doctor_question: When you perform the checking, is it specifically to reduce or prevent the intrusive fear that you may have missed something dangerous?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, exactly. That's the whole reason I do it. I just... I get this awful feeling that I missed something dangerous, and the only way to make it go away is to check. 

That's actually what brings me in, honestly. I just keep going back over jobs again and again. I'm checking the breakers, making sure the labels are right, looking at torque marks... I even take photos of my work to look at later. Sometimes I'll even drive all the way back to a job site after I've left. It's gotten to the point where a simple install takes way longer than it should, and people at work are starting to notice. I just do it to make that fear stop.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in extensive repetitive checking behaviors (inspecting breakers, labels, torque marks, taking photos, and returning to job sites) specifically to reduce the distress and fear of having missed something dangerous.
